A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Synth-SBDH study. All 29 pages of v1 and 34 pages of v2, including appendices, support comparison. Text extraction recovers v1's overflowing appendix lines, allowing their content to be matched despite the rendering defects.

before.justification: V1 reports original classification, entity-recognition, distillation, data-size, and human-evaluation results for Synth-SBDH.

after.justification: V2 retains original experimental and human-evaluation results and adds VA-SBDH classification, alternative pretraining-data comparisons, and Llama evaluations.

M1.justification: The GPT-4 generation pipeline, 45 seed examples, generation prompt, ROUGE-L filtering threshold, and expert review remain unchanged. The sequential fine-tuning and DSS procedures are retained. QLoRA is introduced for additional comparison models, without revising the proposed dataset-generation method.

E1.justification: V2 adds classification of VA-SBDH notes, beyond that corpus's earlier NER evaluation. The underlying datasets, hospital sources, and represented categories remain unchanged. The revised wording '14 SBDH categories and pain' does not remove a category; v1 already included pain and identified it as not an SBDH.

E2.justification: V2 adds Llama 3.2 3B and Llama 3 8B comparisons in Table 14 and MIMIC-SBDHaligned pretraining as an alternative to Synth-SBDH in Table 13. Table 3 drops the standard-fine-tuning Mamba and ClinicalMamba branches, retaining their prompt-based comparisons, although Section 5 still refers to the omitted standard-fine-tuning results.

E3.justification: Table 12 changes the reported downstream NER budget from 40 to 8 epochs. New experiments introduce pretraining with comparable training steps using MIMIC-SBDHaligned versus Synth-SBDH, and QLoRA settings for Llama, including four downstream epochs. Existing splits and exact/relaxed NER metrics remain; relaxed results move to the appendix. These disclosures do not establish which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendix D.2 tests whether synthetic pretraining provides benefits over real-data pretraining with comparable training steps. Conversely, Figure 2 removes the 40-epoch curves and the analysis of interactions between training budget and synthetic-data benefits, retaining the 8-epoch data-size analysis. Rare-category and qualitative annotation-error analyses remain.

E5.justification: V2 newly reports DSS p-values of 0.01 for T5 and 0.36 for FLAN-T5, without specifying the statistical test. Primary comparison tables retain means and standard deviations over three independent runs. There is no explicit increase in run counts.

E6.justification: Table 3 changes prompt-based RoBERTa macro F without/with Synth-SBDH from 56.17/91.20 to 55.64/91.11. Table 4 replaces T5 macro F values of 65.34/67.40 with 25.44/60.73 under the shorter NER budget, rather than demonstrating a same-setting change. V2 also adds classification/Llama results and annotation breakdowns. DSS scores and human-evaluation outcomes remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Neither version develops mathematical theory, formal propositions, or proofs. The retained metric descriptions and annotation-category definitions do not introduce a mathematical change.

C1.justification: V2 adds a cost-advantage claim to the abstract and updates headline improvements to 63.75% macro F and 94.44 absolute F-score points. The NER contribution is narrowed from bringing weaker models near the best in their class to improving Seq2seq models. The central dataset-release, transfer, rationale, and low-resource claims remain.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations concerning T5 training stability, limited Llama gains, and category balance and coverage in the synthetic-versus-real comparison. Human-LLM agreement is newly contextualized against expert disagreement and noisy-label literature. Appendix F adds deployment qualifications and recommends human-labeled data for domain adaptation. The earlier interpretation of benefits under different epoch budgets is removed.

D1.justification: V2 adds annotator qualifications and adjudication details, data-creation cost/time estimates, and Llama-specific QLoRA, hardware, and training information. Table 12 corrects the MLC GPU memory entry from 232GB to 32GB. The already extensive generation prompts, seed examples, annotation guidelines, and code-access information remain.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands cited grounding for clinical utility, category definitions, annotation noise, model adaptation, and synthetic-data biases. Section 2.2 also develops individual accounts of previously cited generation approaches, including GPT3mix and ToxiGen. The central positioning as a larger, openly available SBDH dataset with rationales remains.

P1.justification: V2 makes targeted revisions to the introduction, related-work explanations, results discussion, and terminology, and updates the author list. Limitations and societal impacts move after the conclusion, and new experimental appendices precede the relocated human-evaluation appendix. Much of the original prose and narrative sequence remains intact.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column layout and fixes extensive off-page overflow in seed examples and evaluation prompts. Table 3 is reorganized, relaxed NER results move to an appendix table, human-evaluation summaries are consolidated, and new tables are added. Figure 2 changes panel arrangement, legends, and displayed curves.

improvement.justification: The added real-data pretraining control and VA-SBDH/Llama comparisons better establish the dataset's utility and limits. Annotation-process disclosures and repaired appendix wrapping also improve auditability. These gains are tempered by the removal of the epoch comparison and lingering references to results omitted from Table 3. The larger NER gains arise under a shorter training budget and therefore do not establish stronger performance under the earlier settings.
